summary.intent: Manage the cipher-box milestone dashboard using the GSD manager workflow: clean up stale state, execute/plan/discuss phases 29-32 in parallel, resolve PR reviews, and simplify code across phases 30-31-32.
summary.outcome: Phases 28-32 all executed and planned; PRs #386 (Phase 30), #387 (Phase 31), #388 (Phase 32) created; Phase 29 PR #383 merged; all Phase 29/30 PR review threads resolved; Phase 32 FUSE async implementation drops worst-case blocking from O(N×10s) to O(10s); Phase 31 test coverage improvement and final Phase 30 review fixes still in-flight at transcript end.

repo: FUSE-T uses SMB backend exclusively — NFS has an unfixable macOS kernel bug; single-thread constraint means all FUSE-T callbacks run on one thread
Channel-based prefetch pattern (PendingContent/content_tx/content_rx/prefetching HashSet) is the established pattern for async work on the FUSE thread — Phase 32 mirrors it exactly for FilePointers
drain_refresh_completions() was calling block_with_timeout() sequentially per FilePointer on the FUSE thread, blocking for up to 10s per file (100s for 10 files), causing Finder 'connection lost'
Phase 28 logger exports a mutable transports array; registerFaroTransport() pushes into it at runtime — tight coupling by design for post-init injection
GSD planning artifacts live on branches and in worktrees — manager init reads disk state and can show stale status when planning commits are on a different branch than the working tree
bin.service.ts is already deprecated with only 2 consumers and SDK equivalents exist — D-09/D-15 deferral was correct
unenrollIpns() was returning void despite executing a DELETE; callers summing affected counts were always getting 0

code.finding: drain_refresh_completions() blocked the FUSE thread calling block_with_timeout() sequentially per FilePointer — replaced with tokio::spawn() async tasks
scrubObject depth limit was returning the raw object at depth > 3 instead of a redacted placeholder — security gap
SENSITIVE_KEYS was missing 'email' — added; arrays were not traversed in scrubObject — added array handling

registerFaroTransport was forwarding context to Faro without scrubbing — potential PII/key leakage; also had duplicate context transformation between error/warn branches that was extracted to toStringContext helper
unenrollIpns() returned void; unenrollBatch() summed results as 0 always — fixed return type to number (affected rows)
1206-line file split into 3 hooks (orchestrator 378, actions 478, write ops 378) plus SDK extraction of tree utils, error/retry, share context builder, and TTL key cache

Poll-wait fallback (5s/100ms) added to handle_open() and handle_read() for unresolved FilePointers — returns EIO on timeout (Finder retries automatically); extracted poll loop into wait_for_filepointer_resolution() helper

Source maps should only be 'hidden' (uploaded but not served) when all three env vars are present (VITE_FARO_URL, GRAFANA_FARO_API_KEY, GRAFANA_STACK_ID); missing GRAFANA_STACK_ID check caused potential empty-string stackId

workflow: GSD manager can dispatch plan/execute as background agents and discuss inline simultaneously — effective for parallelizing phase work from one terminal
Worktrees from merged PRs must be explicitly removed; they're not cleaned up automatically and can cause false 'active background' indicators in the dashboard
When a feature branch is ahead of main and both modify ROADMAP.md, always take main's version for the planning sections — main is authoritative for completion status
Phase execution agents in worktrees commit to worktree-specific branches (worktree-agent-XXXX); these need to be pushed to a named feature branch and merged back via PR
prettier --write on the worktree directory after agent execution catches formatting issues before CI; agents don't always run prettier on generated files
The 'resolve PR review comments' workflow correctly distinguishes 'already fixed' vs 'not applicable' vs 'valid fix needed' — prevents redundant fixes for threads posted before earlier commits

friction: ROADMAP.md had repeated merge conflicts across multiple sessions — the three-way conflict format made it easy to accidentally keep both versions
Phase 31 CI failed with 11 prettier formatting errors — agent-generated code wasn't formatted before push
Phase 30 required three separate rounds of PR review resolution (GitHub Copilot → CodeRabbit → second CodeRabbit pass) — each round added new scrubbing security findings
Worktree cleanup caused unexpected branch checkout changes — after removing the Phase 32 planning worktree, the main repo switched to the Phase 32 branch silently
Phase 30 simplify fixes landed on the wrong branch (Phase 32) due to worktree confusion and had to be recovered
The GSD manager's disk-state polling couldn't detect that Phase 30 was already executed in a worktree — showed 'ready to execute' when the work was done but on a different branch
Phase 31 SDK tests had 35 pre-existing type errors unrelated to Phase 31 work — needed a separate fix agent
open_items: Phase 31 test coverage improvement (agent still running at transcript end) — CodeRabbit flagged that SDK error/retry utilities and key-cache had no unit tests
Phase 30 second-round review fixes (URL hex scrubbing, Faro instrumentation privacy config) — commit created but push not confirmed at transcript end
Phase 32 simplify changes in worktree — compiled clean but push not confirmed at transcript end
Phase 33 (Windows WinFsp async FilePointer) — context ready, PR #385 merged to docs branch, but planning and execution deferred pending Phase 32 merge
GitHub Actions secrets VITE_FARO_URL, GRAFANA_FARO_API_KEY, GRAFANA_STACK_ID need to be configured in the staging environment before Faro activates
Cargo.lock discrepancy in Phase 32 worktree from version-bump divergence — left uncommitted, should be rebased onto main after merge
Phase 28 logger module is a missing dependency for faro.ts registerFaroTransport() — main.tsx wiring call is deferred; stringly-typed log level constants can't be imported until Phase 28 ships
Batch IPNS resolve API endpoint noted as future optimization during Phase 32 discussion
